# NSPanel HAUI 0.5.2

Version 0.5.2 fixes several schedule problems, makes the preview's entity hover work everywhere and tidies the editor's forms, Fleet and the Updates sidebar. It includes the Home Assistant integration, editor and firmware; the firmware only carries the new version number, and the display TFT files are unchanged.

## Before updating

One stored setting may change by itself. A schedule entry that sets its own dimmed brightness now needs the device's **Brightness dimmed**. When the integration loads the panel store, it sets **Brightness dimmed** to 20 % (the panel's default) on every device whose schedule needs it and logs a warning. After updating, check the value under **Screen** in the device settings. See [the upgrade notes](docs/user/update.md#a-schedule-entry-that-dims-needs-a-dimmed-brightness).

No TFT update is needed; the release continues to require display version 0.4.5.

## Breaking changes

- **Dimmed brightness for a schedule** — in 0.5.0 a schedule entry could set a dimmed brightness while the device left **Brightness dimmed** empty, to keep the value set on the panel. The hub then had nothing to restore when the entry ended, and the panel kept the entry's dimmed brightness. The device setting is now required for such an entry: it is the dimmed brightness outside the entry. Stored devices are migrated as described above. A configuration that sets an entry's dimmed brightness without the device setting is refused when it is saved. When you give an entry a dimmed brightness in the **Schedule** sidebar while the device has none, the sidebar takes the panel's **Brightness Dimmed** reading (20 % when the panel reports none), says so, and saves it with the schedule.

## Added

- **Selecting a device on Fleet** — select a **Device inventory** row anywhere outside its name and buttons (or press Enter or Space while it has focus), or the name strip under a device card. The row and the card are highlighted together, so a device is easy to find in both, and selecting a row scrolls the cards to it. Select it again to clear the selection. The card's screen still opens the device.
- **Schedule defaults** — the **Schedule** sidebar shows, read-only under **Outside the entries**, the settings that apply between the entries and fill every entry field left empty: brightness (full and dimmed), auto dimming with its timeout and fade, auto display off and the notification sound. Before, the sidebar only said that the device settings apply. **Edit in device settings** opens the device settings with **Screen** and **Sounds** unfolded; closing them returns to the schedule with your unsaved entries.

## Changed

- **Entity names** — Home Assistant puts the device name in front of an entity's full name, so the editor showed names such as *NSPanel Salon Lampa Kuchnia*. The entity picker, item lists, the **Diagnostics** entity list and the preview's entity tooltip now show the entity's own name (*Lampa Kuchnia*). Typing the full name in the entity picker still finds the entity.
- **Switches** — every switch in the editor sits at the right end of its row, after its label: device settings, panel and item options, schedule entries, update settings and the **Device Enabled** switch.
- **Device settings** — each field takes its own row. **Screen** lists the brightness values, timeouts and dimming duration first, then the auto dimming and auto display-off switches; **Home & idle** shows the **Home panel** and **Idle panels** pickers at the right edge of their row, followed by **Auto page** and its timeout.
- **Update settings** — the **Update channel** is a list, and **Install firmware updates automatically** is a switch that replaces **When a new version is found** (**Manual** or **Auto**). It comes after **Check for a new version**. The stored setting (`firmware_auto_update`) is unchanged.
- **Updates sidebar** — an offered firmware or display update turns the installed version into one badge with the version it updates to (`0.5.2 → 0.5.3`), in place of a separate **Update available** badge and the latest-release note. The integration's version moved from its own row to the end of the **Check for updates** row and shows while updates are off too; the integration updates through the Marketplace, so the sidebar has nothing to install for it. On a narrow sidebar (the default width, or a phone) the row reads **Check** and shows the version alone, **Install** shows only its icon and the badge shows only the new version.
- **Fleet layout** — the dashboard uses the full width of a wide window instead of stopping at 1440 px. The **Device inventory** grows with its devices; a long list scrolls under its column headings, which stay in view. **Latest events** beside it takes the inventory's height and scrolls inside it; on a narrow window, where the two cards stack, it keeps a height of its own.
- **Device screen tiles** — the **Connection & device** and **Diagnostics** tiles show their values in smaller text, and the Wi-Fi signal bars stand at the tile's edge beside the label and value instead of after the value.
- **Integration, not hub** — the Updates sidebar and the panel's About page already call the Home Assistant side the *integration*; Fleet and **Diagnostics** now do too. The summary strip on Fleet shows **Integration version** instead of **Hub version**, and **Diagnostics** shows the **Integration log** tile and **Integration details** instead of **Hub log** and **Hub details**. A report made with **Copy report** heads its log lines *Recent integration log*.
- **Panel overview** — with no panel selected, the Panels view's side card shows a tile for the **Home panel** and one for the **Idle panel**. Each tile now shows the role's icon on its left with the role and the panel stacked beside it; before, the panel sat under a row of icon and role. On a narrow card the two tiles stack, so a long panel name keeps its room.

## Fixed

### Schedule

- **Dimmed brightness after an entry** — an entry's dimmed brightness no longer stays after the entry ends; see *Breaking changes*.
- **Auto display off** — saving the device settings with a changed **Auto display off** while an entry was active wrote the panel's switch a second time and could override the entry. While the schedule has entries, it now owns the switch alone. When you remove every entry, the integration sets the switch once from **Auto display off**; after that, automations control it again.
- **Daylight saving time** — on the day the clocks change, the time to the next entry was counted on the wall clock, so an entry could start an hour early or late. It now starts on time.
- **Polar night** — where the sun did not rise or set until the next day, the hub stopped looking for the next sunrise or sunset entry and resumed only after the panel reconnected. It now looks again every day.

### Editor

- **Home Assistant app** — in the Home Assistant app the strip under the phone's status bar showed the page background above the editor's title bar. The editor now handles the screen insets itself: the strip takes the header colour, and the content keeps clear of the screen's side edges and the home indicator.
- **Entity hover on Row panels** — with **Show entities in the preview** on, only a row's icon and name named its entity. The row's buttons, switch and slider now name it too.
- **Entity hover on hardware buttons** — hovering a hardware button in the preview now names the entity it switches: its entity when one is set without relay mode, otherwise its relay.
- **Entity hover in Live mode** — the entity hover worked only in the Simulated preview; in the Live preview it raised an error on every mouse move. The Live preview now names the entity under the mouse as well.
- **Missing entities** — a widget whose entity Home Assistant does not have was not named at all. It is named now, and the tooltip says when an entity is not found or unavailable, which explains why the panel shows it as unavailable.

### Updates

- **Translations** — the reasons a firmware update is withheld or refused (the panel and the release are different build variants, the panel reports no or an invalid firmware version, the manifest names no build variant) and the panel's notice that a firmware release is installing were shown in English only. They are now translated into every device language.
